 Last Update November 7, 2026, 6:02 PM EST Trump says US military carried out 'minor strikes' as Iran reports attack on Qeshm Island
 President Donald Trump declined to say whether the U.S. was responsible for reported strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island, while acknowledging that American forces have conducted limited strikes against Iranian air defenses during Operation Epic Fury.
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on Twitter 
 Share on Flipboard 
 Share by Email 
 WHAT TO KNOW
 The State Department warned Americans in the Middle East to remain vigilant amid increased threats of armed attacks by Iranian-backed Houthi militants in Yemen.
 President Donald Trump said Friday that Iran is eager to reach a deal with the United States, citing economic troubles and damage to Tehran's military capabilities.
 The U.S. is offering a reward of up to $20 million for information about Iran's nuclear program, U.S. Central Command said.
 Qatar pushed back Friday against reports suggesting negotiations between the United States and Iran had collapsed.
 16 Posts Sort by Newest Oldest incoming update… Coverage for this event has ended.
 6 hours ago Pinned US announces task force to monitor weapons, technology moving across Iran’s borders 
 (Photo by Elke Scholiers/Getty Images) The U.S. announced Task Force Iron Gate on Saturday, which is meant to track illegal movement of advanced weapons, dual-use technologies, illegal revenue streams and other sanctioned material over Iran’s border and the Caspian Sea as the U.S. expands its naval blockade .
 The task force will be based in Tampa and coordinate with several U.S. agencies.
 Posted by Brie Stimson Share 6 hours ago US forces disable vessel that violated Iran naval blockade in Gulf of Oman 
 U.S. forces disabled a commercial vessel that attempted to violate the naval blockade in the Gulf of Oman on Saturday, CENTCOM said, adding that the vessel ignored repeated warnings.
 A U.S. military aircraft disabled the St. Kitts-flagged M/V Huda by firing munitions at its stern
 “CENTCOM continues to strictly enforce America’s naval blockade against Iran,” CENTCOM said in a release. “Enforcement actions since July have resulted in U.S. forces redirecting 147 commercial vessels that complied and disabled five merchant ships that refused to comply.”
 CENTCOM added that the U.S. has also destroyed 10 Iranian commercial oil tankers that were part of the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps’ multibillion-dollar shadow network.
 Posted by Brie Stimson Share 7 hours ago Israeli president asks Netanyahu opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form new government 
 Gadi Eisenkot, Israel's former military chief of staff and leader of the Yashar party, addresses supporters at the party's final campaign rally before the legislative election, in Tel Aviv on October 25, 2026. Israel headed to the polls on October 27 in its first election since the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack, in what is seen as a referendum on the prime minister. (Photo by Jack GUEZ / AFP via Getty Images) Israeli President Isaac Herzog announced on Saturday that he has asked Gadi Eisenkot, the leader of the Yashar party — the main party seeking to replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu — to form a government .
 Eisenkot has been invited to the president’s residence on Sunday where he will be asked to form a government following Israel’s contentious elections.
 Herzog held in-depth talks with people across the Israeli political spectrum over the last few days, including Netanyahu.
 Eisenkot will then have 28 days to form a new government under Israeli law.
 Posted by Brie Stimson Share 9 hours ago Qatar, Saudi Arabia working closely to 'strengthen security' in the Middle East 
 Qatar's foreign ministry said Saturday that its foreign minister called his Saudi Arabian counterpart to discuss "ongoing diplomatic efforts and close coordination to achieve de-escalation and strengthen security and stability in the region." 
 It said the call between Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al-Thani and Saudi Arabia's Prince Faisal bin Farhan bin Abdullah Al-Saud "underscored the State of Qatar's support for all diplomatic efforts and endeavors to find a solution that ensures the freedom of maritime navigation and paves the way for reaching a comprehensive accord that achieves enduring peace in the region." 
 The call came as a spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition said early Saturday that Saudi Arabia's air defenses "Intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile launched by the Houthi terrorist militia toward the Riyadh area." 
 Posted by Greg Norman-Diamond Share 9 hours ago Turkey's Erodgan tells Trump to resolve US-Iran war through diplomacy: report 
 Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, right, shakes hands with President Donald Trump upon his arrival at Etimesgut Air Base near Ankara, on July 7, 2026, before attending the 36th NATO Heads of State and Government Summit. (Saul Loeb/AFP via Getty Images) Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan spoke by phone with President Donald Trump and said the conflict between the U.S. and Iran should be resolved through diplomacy, Reuters reported Saturday, citing a statement from Erdogan's office. 
 Erdogan also said Turkey will continue to assist in efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war, the report added. 
 The U.S. launched Operation Epic Fury against Iran on Feb. 28. 
 Posted by Greg Norman-Diamond Share 10 hours ago Gas prices have fallen nearly 15 cents a gallon over the last week, AAA data shows 
 Gas prices are displayed at a Love's gas station in Moody, Ala., on Nov. 4, 2026. (Edgar Su/Reuters) Data from AAA shows that the average price for a regular gallon of gas in the U.S. has fallen nearly 15 cents over the last week. 
 Gas prices have been elevated during the U.S. war against Iran and they were a key issue for voters during this week's midterm elections, where Republicans lost the House and Senate. 
 As of Saturday, it costs on average $4.04 for a gallon of gas in the U.S., down from $4.18 a week ago. 
 One month ago, gas prices were on average $4.37 a gallon, according to AAA. 
 Diesel prices are also slipping at $6.21 a gallon, down from $6.31 last week. 
 Posted by Greg Norman-Diamond Share 11 hours ago Iranian official takes swipe at US after midterms, warns of 'devastating response' 
 Iranian Supreme National Security Council chief Mohsen Rezaei. (Mohammed Salem/Reuters) Iranian Supreme National Security Council chief Mohsen Rezaei took an apparent swipe at the Trump administration on Saturday following this week's midterm elections, writing on X, "You lost the war and the election.
 "Vance has conceded, Rubio is heading for the exit, Hegseth is about to be fired, and the CENTCOM commander is now a podcaster!" he claimed.
 "So٫ who exactly in Washington do we need to get this message across to? Start a war, and you’ll face a devastating response," Rezaei also said.
 Vance said in a post on X following the midterms that "the reason we lost is the war," and, "the president himself said so last night."
 Posted by Greg Norman-Diamond Share 11 hours ago Top Gulf official offers glimmer of hope on Trump-Iran nuclear talks 
 DUBAI, United Arab Emirates — A senior United Arab Emirates official says he is cautiously optimistic about negotiations between the United States and Iran, citing progress through Qatari mediation over the past days, even as fears of renewed military confrontation continue to grip the Middle East.
 "We see some progress. … We hope that both sides will be able to reach a point where they will start building trust and engaging in a way to avoid the war, to find a political solution. … I am a little bit optimistic, but I don't exclude the other option," Dr. Ali Rashid Al Nuaimi, chairman of the Defense, Interior and Foreign Affairs Committee of the UAE's Federal National Council, told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview.
 His remarks came as Reuters reported on Nov. 5 that Iran had submitted a new nuclear proposal to Washington through Qatar. Tehran, however, continued to insist that the U.S. meet seven conditions before negotiations could proceed, including sanctions relief and an end to the American naval blockade.
 President Donald Trump has not ruled out further military operations, while Iran has threatened broader retaliation if fighting resumes.
 For the UAE, which endured thousands of Iranian missile and drone attacks earlier this year, the possibility of a diplomatic breakthrough offers hope. But its leaders are making clear that hope cannot replace preparedness.
 "We plan for the worst. We hope for the best. … We always make sure that we are ready to deal with all the challenges or the threats," Al Nuaimi said.
 Posted by Efrat Lachter Share 12 hours ago UN says more than 313,000 displaced in Yemen fighting since August 
 A man collects plastic bottles at a recent trash dump, which was floodway before the war, in Taiz, Yemen, on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. (Marzouq Al Jabri/AP) The United Nations' Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said more than 313,000 people have now been displaced in fighting in Yemen since the start of August. 
 The figure comes as the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen have been clashing with Saudi-backed government forces.  
 "Taiz Governorate has taken in the largest share, with more than two in five of those displaced seeking shelter there," OCHA said. 
 "Civilians continue to pay the price. The UN Human Rights Office has verified 281 civilian casualties since the beginning of August, with 69 people killed and 212 injured. Children account for more than a third of those casualties," it added. 
 Posted by Greg Norman-Diamond Share 13 hours ago CENTCOM launches Task Force Iron Gate to crack down on 'illegal shipments' to Iran 
 A U.S. Navy MH-60R Sea Hawk takes off from the flight deck of USS George Washington, one of the ships in the Middle East that is enforcing an Iranian port blockade, in this photo released by U.S. Central Command on Oct. 31. (CENTCOM) U.S. Central Command announced Saturday that it launched a task force "that will support ongoing U.S. government efforts to prevent Iran from using ground routes to transport advanced weapons and other materials." 
 "Adm. Brad Cooper has directed the formation of Task Force Iron Gate, an internal staff of approximately 20 civilian and military personnel based in Tampa, Florida," CENTCOM said a statement. "The new CENTCOM team will coordinate with other U.S. government agencies on preventing the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials, and illegal revenue streams across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea." 
 CENTCOM said the ongoing U.S. military blockade of Iranian ports has so far prevented Iran from exporting $25 billion in crude oil. 
 "The establishment of Task Force Iron Gate reinforces the success of our ironclad blockade against Iran at sea," added Cooper, the commander of CENTCOM. "Strengthening CENTCOM's collaboration with U.S. interagency partners will further constrain Iran's ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, and replenish their military."
 Posted by Greg Norman-Diamond Share 13 hours ago Iran claims its military is 'stronger' since Operation Epic Fury began 
 Iranian Army spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia claimed Saturday that the country's military is "stronger" now than when it began the war against the U.S. in February, a report said.
 “Today, the Islamic Republic’s armed forces… having gained experience from direct confrontation with the United States and the Israeli regime, are on higher alert and are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war. They now possess greater motivation, commitment, and self-confidence,” Akraminia told Iran's IRNA news agency, according to the AFP.
 The remarks come despite the U.S. saying Iran has suffered heavy military losses during the war.
 Trump said in June that Iran has "been defeated militarily, with no Navy or Air Force."
 Posted by Greg Norman-Diamond Share 14 hours ago US offers up to $20 million reward for information on Iran's nuclear program 
 The U.S. is offering a reward of up to $20 million and possible relocation assistance for information about Iran's nuclear program, U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) announced Friday.
 In a post on X, CENTCOM highlighted the State Department's Rewards for Justice program, which is seeking information about Iran's nuclear facilities, equipment and personnel involved in the program.
 The reward also covers information about the movement of nuclear-related materials, equipment or personnel, including individuals in the scientific community.
 The announcement comes as President Donald Trump considers renewed military strikes against Iran while Washington and Tehran continue negotiations over the country's nuclear program.
 Trump reiterated Friday that Iran would never be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon, pointing to previous U.S. military operations targeting Tehran's nuclear facilities.
 Posted by Brittany Miller Share 14 hours ago Iran pushes for Middle East security arrangements 'without interference from extra-regional powers' 
 Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi looks over during a meeting with his Russian counterpart in Tehran on Oct. 19, 2026. (Atta Kenare/AFP via Getty Images) Iran's foreign ministry said Saturday that Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi urged countries in the Middle East to set up "regional security arrangements without interference from extra-regional powers." 
 Araghchi wrote on his Telegram account that, "over the past 48 hours, in separate telephone conversations with 12 of my counterparts from Oman, Egypt, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Cyprus, Turkey, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Tunisia, Iraq, and Pakistan, we reviewed and exchanged views on the latest regional and international developments and the consequences of the escalating actions" of the U.S. and Israel.  
 "In these consultations, while explaining the principled positions of the Islamic Republic of Iran, I emphasized the need to respect the national sovereignty of countries, stop aggression and threats, avoid destructive foreign interventions, and the responsibility of regional countries in preventing the spread of insecurity," Araghchi wrote. 
 "I also emphasized our country's legitimate right to defend its sovereignty and national security and the need to form regional security arrangements without the intervention of extra-regional powers," he also said. 
 Posted by Greg Norman-Diamond Share 15 hours ago Iranian lawmaker calls for changes to negotiating team, blames 'lack of precision' 
 Iranian lawmaker Mahmoud Nabavian called on Tehran Saturday to switch up the negotiating team that is trying to reach a deal with the U.S. to end the war. 
 "Given the failed experiences of negotiations with the United States, which, due to a lack of precision and wishful thinking about the enemy, have led to considerable losses, and given that, unfortunately, former members are also involved in the current negotiations, we respectfully request that the esteemed Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council reconsider the composition of the negotiating team under the current sensitive circumstances," Nabavian wrote on X. 
 Qatar, who has been acting as a mediator between both sides, pushed back Friday against reports suggesting negotiations between the U.S. and Iran had collapsed, insisting that both countries are continuing efforts to reach an agreement. 
 Fox News Digital's Brittany Miller contributed to this post.  
 Posted by Greg Norman-Diamond Share 15 hours ago Iran's IRGC says its ballistic missile range limit has been 'lifted for us' 
 Iran IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi speaks during a press conference in Tehran, Iran, on Sept. 29, 2026. (Fatemeh Bahrami/Anadolu via Getty Images) Iranian Gen. Hossein Mohebbi claimed Saturday that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' (IRGC) self-proclaimed limit of 1,200 miles on the range of its ballistic missiles has been "lifted for us." 
 Mohebbi made the remark during a news conference in Tehran where he was asked about the limit on missile ranges. Iran is not known to have missiles that can go beyond the 1,200-mile limit — a range that puts parts of Greece and the Balkans, the entire Arabian Peninsula, the Levant and most of Egypt within reach, according to The Associated Press. 
 “That restriction has been lifted for us," Mohebbi reportedly said. 
 He did not say whether Iran had missiles capable of exceeding the limit, saying only Iran would “demonstrate these capabilities in practice” rather than make statements. 
 The comments come after Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei called on Iran last Saturday to confront any threat "with an immediate, effective, and unrestricted geographical response."   
 The Associated Press contributed to this post.  
 Posted by Greg Norman-Diamond Share 16 hours ago Trump declines to confirm US role in reported strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island 
 President Donald Trump arrives to deliver remarks at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in Washington, D.C., on Nov. 2, 2026. (Umit Bektas/Reuters) President Donald Trump declined Friday to say whether the U.S. was responsible for reported missile strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island, while acknowledging that American forces have conducted limited strikes against Iranian air defenses.
 Asked by a reporter whether the U.S. carried out the reported strikes, Trump responded, "I don't want to talk about it. We do minor strikes, but they knock out. They built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device, and we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five."
 Iranian state media reported that two projectiles struck the Suza area of Qeshm Island, according to Reuters.
 Trump did not specify where the U.S. operation he described took place or whether it was connected to the reported strikes on Qeshm Island.
 Yesterday's Fox News Digital live blog offers additional coverage of the conflict with Iran.
